title: Constructible-image criterion for countable-dimensional norm coefficient projection
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite normed extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and a nonarchimedean normed extension field $F/E$ with the same restricted norm. Assume that the $E$-vector space $F$ is algebraically spanned by at most countably many vectors. Put $A(P)=C(P,E)$, $B(P)=C(P,F)$ on profinite sets using ALL continuous functions, with the inclusion $A\to B$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. For schemes $Z$ put $A_Z=p_Z^*A$, $B_Z=p_Z^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules, ordinary unbounded derived categories, and ordinary K-flat extension $T_Z=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $X$ be any scheme, let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism, and let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_X})$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Set $M=Rf_{*,A}K$ and $N=Rf_{*,B}T_XK$.

For either coefficient field $G=E,F$, a module on $Y$ is called constant-model constructible if, on a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification], it is pro-etale locally $G_Y\otimes_G V$ for a finite-dimensional abstract $G$-vector space $V$ [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Assume that $M$ and $T_YM$ have bounded constant-model constructible cohomology, and that every $H^q(N)$, for $q\in\mathbf Z$, is constant-model constructible; no common cohomological bound on $N$ is assumed.

Define $\beta_{f,K}:T_YM\to N$ as the geometric-adjunction transpose of $f_B^*T_YM\cong T_Xf_A^*M\xrightarrow{T_X\varepsilon}T_XK$, using the canonical balanced tensor comparison [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Then $N$ has bounded constant-model constructible cohomology and this specified $\beta_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_Y})$. More precisely, $H^q(N)=0$ whenever $H^q(M)=0$. Properness, finite type over a field, completeness of $F$, and flatness of $A\to B$ are not hypotheses.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-countable-normed-orthogonal-basis] to the normed $E$-space $F$ with prescribed $b_0=1$. The field norm is homogeneous and ultrametric, $1\ne0$, and the spanning hypothesis is exactly countability. Obtain its uniformly bounded finite-support basis and continuous coordinate $\lambda_0:F\to E$, with $\lambda_0(1)=1$. Set $D=\operatorname{End}^{\mathrm{cts}}_E(F)$ and $e(w)=\lambda_0(w)1$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted countable endomorphism argument, assembly step 1

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-norm-coefficient-endomorphism-corner] with this $\lambda_0$ and the specified balanced comparison. It gives the unital $E$-algebra action of $D$ on $r_YN$, and $M\xrightarrow{\iota}r_YN\xrightarrow{\tau}M$ with $\tau\iota=1$ and $\iota\tau=\rho(e)$. On degree-$q$ fibres, $\iota$ therefore identifies $H^q\Phi_{y,E}(M)$ with $eH$, where $H=H^q\Phi_{y,F}(N)$. Under this identification, the actual fibre of the specified $\beta_{f,K}$ is $F\otimes_E eH\to H$, $v\otimes h\mapsto\theta_vh$. The induced $E$-action agrees with restriction of the $F$-action, since $\rho(m_v)$ is multiplication by $v$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted countable endomorphism argument, assembly step 2

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$ and an algebraically closed geometric point $y$. Ultrametric balls are clopen and separate distinct points, so both fields have totally disconnected topology. Exactness and finite-model detection in [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres] give $H=\Phi_{y,F}(H^qN)$ finite-dimensional over $F$. If $h_1,\ldots,h_r$ span $H$ over $F$, the vectors $b_jh_i$ span it over $E$, a finite or countable family. With the compatible unital $D$-module structure of step 2 and the basis bounds of step 1, [lem-sfb-countable-endomorphism-module-reconstruction] makes $F\otimes_E eH\to H$ invertible. This is precisely $H^q\Phi_y(\beta_{f,K})$ by step 2; its $D$-linearity implies $F$-linearity by taking $d=m_v$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted countable endomorphism argument, assembly step 3

proof.text: If $H^q(M)=0$, exactness of $\Phi_{y,E}$ gives $eH=0$. Step 3 then gives $\Phi_{y,F}(H^qN)=H=0$ for every $y$. Apply the bounded constructible conservativity clause of [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres] to $H^q(N)[0]\to0$: both complexes have bounded finite constant-model constructible cohomology by the hypotheses. Every fibre is zero, so $H^q(N)=0$. Since $M$ has cohomology in a finite interval, so does $N$; each of its cohomology sheaves is constructible by assumption.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent-extracted countable endomorphism argument, assembly step 4

proof.text: Now both $T_YM$ and $N$ have bounded constant-model constructible cohomology. Step 3 makes every cohomology map of every derived fibre of $\beta_{f,K}$ invertible. Each derived fibre is therefore an isomorphism. Bounded constructible conservativity of [lem-sfb-constructible-normed-geometric-fibres] gives that the specified $\beta_{f,K}$ itself is an isomorphism.

Only the wording of steps 2 and 3 changed: iota induces the identification of H^qPhi_E(M) with eH, the E-action is the restriction of the F-action through rho(m_v), and F-linearity follows by taking d=m_v. There are no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and not weakened. Dropping the restriction def from stmt_deps is correct because the statement never uses restriction. I read all four cited statements in full. The corner node has been split since e1b4 with its statement unchanged; the other three nodes are unchanged. Step 1: the basis node applies with V=F and b0=1, so lambda0(1)=1 and lambda0 is continuous. Step 2: the corner node's beta is the item's own normalized beta; it gives the unital D-action, tau iota=1, iota tau=rho(e), the fibre of M identified with eH, and the fibre of beta as v⊗h↦theta_v h. Step 3: ultrametric norms make both fields totally disconnected. By t-exactness and the Noetherian, constant-model hypotheses, H is finite-dimensional over F, so the b_j h_i give a countable E-span. Reconstruction (its lambda0 is the same coordinate) then makes every H^qPhi_y(beta) invertible. Step 4: H^qM=0 gives eH=0, hence H=0, and conservativity applied to H^qN[0]→0 gives H^qN=0, so N is bounded before conservativity is used on it. Step 5: bounded constructible conservativity makes beta an isomorphism. Edge cases checked: F=E, finite [F:E], H=0, Y empty and gaps in the degrees of M. All proof_deps are in unit sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability, there is no cycle, the single citer is unchanged and there is no SGA.
